mentl/85c653e:
The orphan-claims facet named ic_fixpoint_handler on its first run: 3,245
bytes of prose, zero references, the largest claim in the wheel. The
question banked with it was built-ahead or abandoned, since deleting might
have removed the only implementation of §2's cached cursor.

The answer is neither, and only reading the arm gives it. Both branches
called cursor_argmax_compute(caret) — identically. The last_epoch state was
written and never affected a result. The memoization its prose described
did not exist; the handler was a no-op wrapper around what cursor_default
already does.

Two false claims in one comment block: "Installed via ~> above" (installed
nowhere) and "on a stable epoch it resumes the terminal cursor and STOPS
re-projecting" (it re-projected either way). Fourth comment this session
asserting a consumer or behaviour the artifact refutes, and the first one a
verb found instead of a hand read.

Deleting costs no capability. Keeping it was the risk: an unbuilt thing is
honest, while a built-looking thing that silently does nothing is worse
than an absence, because the next person installs it on the strength of the
prose and believes IC is live.

Why it was never finished is the part worth keeping, and it lives at the
deletion site and in RESIDUE: an epoch alone cannot key this read.
cursor_argmax takes a caret, and moving the caret without editing leaves
the graph epoch unchanged while the correct cursor differs — so a
stable-epoch cache answers the wrong position the first time a human moves
without typing. The key is (epoch, caret); the peer is
Hβ.cursor.cached-argmax-keyed-by-epoch-and-caret, and its gate is a fixture
that moves the caret at a stable epoch and proves the answer changes.

The comment-ref ratchet then caught my own prose twice, backticking a name
I had just deleted and a residue id. Both are prose; the backticks came
off.

mentl/85f73d0:
The plan marks Phase 0 complete with the SYNTAX conformance battery as
one of its four landings, and tripwire 3 names that battery as the
standing counter-measure for the oracle-blind class. It did not exist.
Measured three ways: the path has no history under any ref, no gate names
it, and the LEDGER the phase points at for full mechanics has no entry
for it. The 27-fixture run behind the tripwire was a one-off whose
fixtures never landed, which is why its findings had to be rediscovered
by hand while three iterations probed that class manually.

`mentl test <dir>` already reads each fixture's expect header, so this
needed fixtures and a verify leg rather than a new script.

The leg was built wrong first and the RED check caught it. Its first
draft read `mentl test` alone and passed against a deliberately falsified
expectation, because that verb reports the declared value beside the WAT
and judges only the compile side. A gate that cannot fail is what Law 11
exists for. It runs each fixture through run-micro.sh now, and the
falsified contract fails with exit=12 expected=11.

The sweep found two defects, each isolated to one variable, both on
surfaces the wheel never writes. A record pattern whose receiver is a
function parameter reads the wrong field silently: {zeta} over
{alpha: 7, zeta: 9} answers 7, while the same pattern over a local
receiver answers 9. The rest binding traps through a parameter even when
the residual is never read, where the same body over a local receiver
answers 12. Separately, an as-pattern defeats exhaustiveness — a match
covering both variants of a two-variant ADT is refused, and deleting the
binder alone runs clean.

A theory died on the way: "record patterns bind by position" was refuted
by the next probe, since the local-receiver case answers the correct
field where a positional read could not. That wrong theory would have
sent a fix into the record layout.

Three fixtures land green with measured contracts — labeled arguments
fully lab

mentl/8576489:
verify.nx grows from 62-line ledger to three-valued discharge of the
decidable subset of Predicate. predicate_decide returns Some(true) |
Some(false) | None over PTrue/PEq/PLt/PLeq/PAnd/POr/PNot/PCall,
short-circuiting via and_decide / or_decide / not_decide so partial
decidability still folds into Some when one branch dominates.

PEq/PLt/PLeq decide Some(true|false) only when both PExpr leaves are
kind-matched constants (PInt-PInt / PFloat-PFloat / PString-PString
for PEq); cross-kind PEq returns Some(false); PVar / PApp / PCall
fall through to None — defer to ledger or the Arc F.1 verify_smt swap.

The verify_ledger arm now: try predicate_decide; Some(true) → no
debt; Some(false) → report_refinement_rejected at the construction
site (E_RefinementRejected); None → ledger entry as before. The Arc
F.1 swap targets the undecidable arm; the decidable arm here stays
load-bearing across the swap.

Primitive #6 (refinement types) is no longer pure deferral.
mentl/8508417:
Per TH walkthrough: threading IS an effect. Thread declares
spawn/join/current_id/num_cores; SharedMemory declares atomics +
wait/notify; parallel_compose handler intercepts >< branches and
dispatches to OS threads via wasi-threads. sequential_compose is
the SAB-unavailable fallback per Q-B.7.1.

Per Q-B.7.3: >< output order preserved regardless of completion
order — multi-core determinism by construction.

Per INSIGHTS L1346 (Handler IS the Backend): no backends, only
handlers. The threading "library" is two effects + one handler
over the existing >< topology. Same source — single-threaded
baseline OR multi-core scale-out — depending only on the ~> chain.

RmwOp + WaitResult are ADTs (drift mode 3 — not string-keyed).
Handle is opaque (drift mode 7 — handler state is List<Handle>,
not parallel arrays).

Composes with race (HC2 §7.3): forks GENUINELY execute across
cores when both installed; race's tiebreak preserves determinism.
Composes with Choice (CE): per-option exploration parallelizable.
Composes with arena_ms: per-thread bump_allocator + replay_safe /
fork_deny / fork_copy compose with thread-local arenas.

FFI surface (ffi_spawn, ffi_join, ffi_current_thread_id,
ffi_num_cores) declares the shape; full bodies invoke wasi-threads
imports as peer handle TH.W.

tokensafe/853e63b:
Phase 5 of the monetization roadmap. Agents register callback URLs +
mint lists via Bearer-auth CRUD endpoints. Background job polls watched
mints on a configurable interval (default 5min) and delivers HMAC-SHA256
signed POST payloads when risk thresholds are exceeded.

Architecture: SQLite via better-sqlite3 (zero-config, works with Railway
persistent volume) over Redis ($8+/mo add-on). Synchronous API keeps the
CRUD layer simple. Delivery retries with exponential backoff (1m, 5m,
then abandoned after 3 attempts).

New routes (before x402 gate, Bearer-auth protected):
  POST /v1/webhooks — register subscription
  GET /v1/webhooks — list (secret redacted)
  PATCH /v1/webhooks/:id — update
  DELETE /v1/webhooks/:id — delete

New files: db.ts (schema + CRUD), webhook-delivery.ts (HMAC + retry),
monitor-job.ts (background polling via checkTokenLite).
